title: Rotating Assembly Callout Map
description: Schematic side cross-section of an overhung (Arrangement 1 style) fan with ten rotating-assembly callouts. Explore mode opens what each part does; quiz mode hides the labels and shows the ten job descriptions in shuffled order, two attempts each, then reports the first-try score against a mastery level of 8 of 10. Schematic, not to scale.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of an overhung fan's rotating assembly
learningObjectives: The learner will identify ten parts of an overhung fan's rotating assembly, given a one-sentence description of each part's job.

accessibility.notes: Every part is a focusable role=button; Tab walks the parts from the shaft sleeve to the keyway, Enter or Space selects one, and after an answer focus moves to Next, so Enter goes on. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an "Answer" badge pair with colour. During the quiz part names are hidden from screen readers too until revealed. When the drawing is narrower than about 650 px the callouts switch to numbers with a key list.

rules: Explore mode: clicking a callout shows its description; any number of clicks; never scored.
Quiz mode: the 10 descriptions appear once each in shuffled order; two attempts each; a click on the matching part is correct.
A first wrong click names the clicked part and its job; a second wrong click highlights the answer and the item counts as missed.
Clicking a non-callout area does nothing and uses no attempt.
Running count 'Correct on first try: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt; Start over reshuffles.
assumptions: Overhung (Arrangement 1 style) layout: impeller outboard of both bearings, sheave on the drive end.
limitations: Schematic, not to scale, not a specific Twin City Fan model. The bearing seal callout marks the inboard bearing's seals; the drive end bearing has them too.

sources: FanPedia (Twin City Fan, 2021): shaft p. 79; keyways and turndowns p. 80; turndown locations p. 81; shaft collar and sleeve p. 129; drive end and inboard bearing names p. 91; bearing seals p. 100; vibration sensor tap p. 101; bearing positioner p. 102 and p. 176
Chapter 16 spec 'Content' table: callout labels and infobox texts

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labeled callouts first, then retrieval practice: name each part from its job with the labels hidden, with immediate correction.
keyQuestions: Which seal keeps air in the housing, and which keeps dirt out of the bearing?
Which bearing is nearer the sheave?
commonMisconceptions: The shaft sleeve is a bearing part.
The shaft locking collar and a bearing's locking collar are the same part.
The shaft seal keeps grease in the bearing.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt; running line 'Correct on first try: n of 10'.
